verdict: Revise once more before round 1's questions go out; no blocker. The revision answers the first review well: of its 18 issues, 16 are resolved and 2 partly (issues 0 and 6), and of the lead's items, L1 to L7 are resolved and L8 partly. What was checked and holds: `design.md` is byte-identical to the render of a copy of `design/`, render.py's consistency checks pass and the copy's JSON comes out unchanged; the quote checker finds 0 prose runs and 0 runs of names in `design.md` and in each of the 16 files under `design/`; none of them has a user or host name or an e-mail address, and the only absolute path is a generic one in a comment of `design/tools/run.sh` (N15); every question has its round, its D-007 mark and a one-sentence summary, two to four sentences of question and one to three per option; each question's Blocks equals the packages whose Blocked-by names it; the acceptance path is WP00a, WP01, WP02, WP03, WP04, WP06, WP08, WP09a, WP10 and WP11a, with round-1 questions only; the code claims match their `file:line`s, except one citation; the numbers trace to their records, except the claim about rate changes below; D-002, D-007, D-046, D-050, D-068, D-069 and D-070 are respected; `<repo>` is at `75cf6e0` and clean. Two major problems remain. (1) The revised check of Q02 (d)'s seconds compares each frame step with one frame duration within half a frame, so it does not catch a change of frame rate, although §4.2, Q02 (d), R11 and WP01's test say it does: with testgen's ad re-timed at 24, 30 and 50 fps it flags nothing while (d)'s seconds end 0.083, 0.333 and 1.000 s away from (c)'s (`runs/rate-change-check.txt`), so the comparison of (c) and (d) that Q02 asks of the owner rests on a safeguard that covers missing frames only. (2) WP01, in round 1, is to implement and test attribution on a session's curve, whose `Span` and `Session` types WP00b declares in round 2 after WP01 has merged, and no later package owns that code. Thirteen minor issues follow (§2, N3 to N15). The records of this review are in `<out>/review-2/runs/`, made with `<out>/review-2/tools/run.sh`, a copy of `design/tools/run.sh` that differs from it in one comment, reworded for N15.

issues.issue: N1: The revised axis check doesn't catch a change of frame rate. The check compares each step between consecutive reference frames with one frame duration, within half a frame. By its own rule, a reference whose frames come at any rate from two thirds to twice its declared rate passes every step, while (d)'s seconds, the frame index times the declared duration, drift. With testgen's ad report re-timed so that the ad's frames 75 to 124 come at 24, 30 or 50 fps (simulated, the playlist's EXTINF following the media), the design's own `axis_check.py` flags 0 steps with the segment map, and (d)'s seconds end 0.083, 0.333 and 1.000 s away from (c)'s after the ad; only 60 fps is flagged, at 49 steps (`runs/rate-change-check.txt`). RFC 8216 expects an `EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY` where encoding parameters change ([§4.3.2.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8216#section-4.3.2.3)), so an ad at another rate after one is a stream the check must expect. §4.2, Q02 (d), R11 and WP01's test say the check warns at a change of rate; the test as specified passes only for changes outside those bounds. Q02 asks the owner to weigh (c) against a checked (d), and the agent's recommendation rests on the check covering both failures it names.
issues.suggestion: Bound the accumulated error, not the step. The check needs the segment map anyway, so compare (d)'s seconds with the playlist time at each segment's first frame, or each frame's PTS with the PTS expected from the first frame of its playlist discontinuity sequence, flagged beyond half a frame. In the same simulation the first form flags 4 segment starts at 24, 30, 50 and 60 fps and none on the unchanged ladder (`runs/rate-change-check.txt`). Then correct §4.2, Q02 (d) and its "Why", K2, R11 and WP01's test, and let the owner compare (c) and (d) on that basis.
